references.citation: Lim, L. F. and Nittler, L. R. (2009), Elemental composition of 433 Eros: New calibration of the NEAR-Shoemaker XRS data, Icarus 200, 129-146
references.locator: Table 9, 'Uncorrected elemental ratios' column (average of eight solar flares); the same values are in the abstract
references.instrument: NEAR-Shoemaker X-ray spectrometer (XRS), orbital X-ray fluorescence during eight solar flares, 2000 May 4 to 2001 January 2
references.footprint: Whole-body average: each flare sampled the sunlit part of Eros in the field of view; the paper states the averaged composition 'probably represents the light-element composition of the whole of Eros' and that the XRS data alone can neither establish nor rule out spatial variation (section 7).
references.samplingDepth: Top tens to hundreds of micrometres (section 7)
references.note: Uncertainties as published in Table 9: photon statistics combined with the spread over plausible solar-spectrum models. No mineral-mixing correction applied; the corrected column (Mg/Si 0.783, Fe/Si 2.383) is not used. Supersedes the calibration of Nittler et al. (2001), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1945-5100.2001.tb01856.x, whose results the paper finds consistent within uncertainties.

references.citation: Peplowski, P. N., Bazell, D., Evans, L. G., Goldsten, J. O., Lawrence, D. J. and Nittler, L. R. (2015), Hydrogen and major element concentrations on 433 Eros, Meteoritics & Planetary Science 50, 353-367
references.locator: Table 2, 'This study' BGO column (abundance ratios); hydrogen from the abstract and the Hydrogen Abundance section
references.instrument: NEAR gamma-ray spectrometer, BGO anticoincidence shield, on the surface after the 2001 February 12 landing
references.footprint: Landing site only: after the landing the instrument was 'just centimeters from the surface' (Methods). The paper describes the site as a ponded regolith deposit (Veverka et al. 2001).
references.note: Uncertainties are 2 standard deviations, statistical and systematic, as the Table 2 footnote states. The paper reports weight ratios ('Our reported weight ratios, listed in Table 2'). It reuses the potassium abundance of Evans et al. (2001) rather than remeasuring it.

references.citation: Evans, L. G. et al. (2001), Elemental composition from gamma-ray spectroscopy of the NEAR-Shoemaker landing site on 433 Eros, Meteoritics & Planetary Science 36, 1639-1660
references.locator: Table 1, K(1461) row, Anticoincidence column: 'Composition 0.07%'; uncertainty from the text before the Discussion ('we assume that this 40% uncertainty applies for all the GRS results')
references.instrument: NEAR gamma-ray spectrometer, NaI detector, on the surface after the 2001 February 12 landing
references.note: Peplowski et al. (2015) quote the same result as 700 ppm.
